back: in fact / really. 'Actualmente' = currently / at the moment
example: Actually, I've changed my mind. / Currently, I work in Madrid.

back: in the end, after a long time. 'Eventualmente' = possibly / occasionally
example: We eventually found the hotel.
Over 300 people attended the conference.
I was so embarrassed when I tripped.
That's a sensible decision. / She's very sensitive.

back: understand, become aware of. 'Realizar' = carry out, do
example: The researchers carried out a survey.

back: act as if something is true. 'Pretender' = intend, aim
example: What do you intend to do?
I bought it at a bookshop.
Save it in this folder.
I've got a cold.
The launch was a huge success.
She works in a car factory.
It was a very long meeting.
I did a degree in economics.

back: go to (an event). 'Atender' = serve / deal with / pay attention
example: The waiter served us quickly.

back: a conversation about a topic. 'Discusión' (fight) = argument
example: They had a terrible argument.

back: showing understanding of someone's problems. 'Simpático' = nice / friendly
example: Her new boss is really nice.
That's just a cliché about Spaniards.
Stir the soup.
Can I give you some advice? / a warning sign

back: abuse sexually - AVOID! 'Molestar' = bother / disturb / annoy
example: Sorry to bother you.
I can't stand this noise.
Please reply to my email.

back: a disagreement OR a line of reasoning. 'Argumento' (of a film) = plot
example: The plot of the film is confusing.
Reading is my favourite hobby.
